sudodrift takes a snapshot of the things that decide who can do what on a Linux machine, then compares two snapshots and tells you what changed. It covers users and groups, SSH key fingerprints, sudo rules, sshd settings, SUID and SGID files, world-writable files and permissions on sensitive files. It only reads. It never changes the host it scans.

This is the first release under the name sudodrift. The project was called permdrift in v0.1.0. I renamed it because another project already uses the name PermDrift, and I removed the v0.1.0 release because its binaries carry the old name. The module path, the command name, the default directory (`/var/lib/sudodrift`) and the environment variables (`SUDODRIFT_*`) all changed.

What is new in 0.2.0

- `sudodrift diff --format text|json|csv`. Text is still the default. JSON and CSV are meant for scripts and spreadsheets. The exit codes are the same for every format: 0 no drift, 1 drift, 2 error.
- `sudodrift evidence` writes a zip (or a directory with `--dir`) with both snapshots, the diff in text and JSON, the HTML report, metadata, a review form and a `MANIFEST.sha256` file you can check with `sha256sum -c`. It collects material for a review. It is not a signature and not a compliance result.
- Examples for running it on a schedule: a systemd service and timer, a cron file, a snapshot script that keeps dated files, and a check script that exits non-zero on drift.

Install

    VER=v0.2.0; ARCH=amd64   # or arm64
    curl -fsSLO https://github.com/sudodrift/sudodrift/releases/download/$VER/sudodrift_${VER#v}_linux_$ARCH.tar.gz
    curl -fsSLO https://github.com/sudodrift/sudodrift/releases/download/$VER/SHA256SUMS
    sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS --ignore-missing
    tar xzf sudodrift_${VER#v}_linux_$ARCH.tar.gz
    sudo install -m 0755 sudodrift /usr/local/bin/

Or with Go: `go install github.com/sudodrift/sudodrift/cmd/sudodrift@latest`

Known limits: the evidence manifest is a list of checksums, so anyone who can rewrite the bundle can rewrite the manifest. The systemd units pass `systemd-analyze verify` but have not run for a full week on a real server. The arm64 build was not run on arm64 hardware.

Full list of changes is in CHANGELOG.md.
